sections.h2: Selling a house in Elizabeth, NJ
sections.html:
Elizabeth is a dense port city: 141,675 residents on 12.32 square miles of land, about 11,145 people per square mile by the 2020 count. Only 25.6 percent of homes are owner occupied, so many houses for sale are two, three and four family buildings that investors and live-in owners both compete for. Median value of owner-occupied homes is $449,300, median gross rent is $1,523, and median household income is $66,555.

Price realistically against that $449,300 median rather than against figures from richer Union County suburbs. A bilingual listing, flyer and contract summary can reach more of the buyers in this city.

The city sits in Union County between Newark to the north and Linden to the southwest. Newark Bay and the Arthur Kill form its eastern edge. The street plan is unusual for New Jersey: instead of a grid, it is largely circular, with streets radiating from the central railroad station. A house a block from Elizabeth station and one near Warinanco Park are very different propositions, so a good listing names the neighborhood and the number of units in the first line.

Elizabeth neighborhoods buyers ask about

Frog HollowSmall pocket of homes east of Atlantic Street near the Arthur Kill

Elizabeth has an online Resale Certificates application, and the form asks you to attach the smoke detector certificate if the property is occupied. Call the Bureau of Zoning for the current fee and inspection timing when you submit it.

Use these detector rules as a checklist before you apply:

  • Smoke detectors on every level, including the basement and any finished attic, mounted at the center of the ceiling within ten feet of bedrooms.
  • A carbon monoxide detector on every floor near sleeping areas, with combination units allowed.
  • A UL listed 2-A:10-B:C fire extinguisher, fully charged and mounted within ten feet of the stove in every kitchen.
  • Hardwired systems must have power on and all units sounding together; battery units cannot replace a hardwired system.

Everything has to be mounted and working before the inspector arrives.

NJ Transit stops at Elizabeth station and North Elizabeth on the Northeast Corridor and North Jersey Coast lines, with service to Newark Penn, Secaucus Junction and New York Penn. Buses run to the Port Authority terminal and to Newark. By road, the New Jersey Turnpike, Interstate 278, U.S. 1 and 9, and Routes 27, 28, 81 and 439 all cross the city, and The Mills at Jersey Gardens anchors retail. Mean travel to work is 26.7 minutes. The Goethals Bridge lands here on the way to Staten Island, and the Port Newark Elizabeth Marine Terminal and part of Newark Liberty airport sit within the city, so buyers who work in logistics or at the airport often search here first. Say how far the house is from the station or the Turnpike, because commuters compare those two first.

Elizabeth Public Schools is one of 31 former Abbott districts, with five new academies and a smaller Elizabeth High School. Mention the zoned school in your listing, and confirm it with the district first, since buyers with children will ask before they book a showing.

• The current block and lot numbers, confirmed with the Tax Assessor, since the city renumbered parcels starting January 1, 2023.
  • Proof of working, mounted detectors and extinguishers for every unit, ready for the smoke certificate attached to the resale application.
  • Permit records for any finished basement, converted attic or added unit, plus any boiler, roof or electrical paperwork.
  • Tenant names, lease terms and security deposit records if the building is occupied.
  • The deed, mortgage payoff figure and any lien letters.

Having all of this in one folder shortens the time between accepting an offer and sending a contract package to the buyer's attorney.

Deeds are recorded with the Union County Clerk, whose land records site is clerk.ucnj.org. A notice there says the city began assigning new lot and block numbers on January 1, 2023, and that the person preparing the deed must confirm the correct numbers with the Tax Assessor or the county tax board association before recording. The clerk is not responsible for numbers copied from an old document.

On the state side, the seller pays the realty transfer fee on the deed. Rates run per $500 of price and step up in bands, and sales over $1,000,000 add a graduated percent fee. A seller who is a New Jersey resident signs GIT/REP-3. Sellers who are nonresidents use GIT/REP-1 or GIT/REP-2 unless a listed assurance applies. Appeals of an assessment must reach the county board of taxation by April 1.

sections.h2: How an Elizabeth sale usually unfolds
sections.html:
Start with the property record: confirm the block and lot with the Tax Assessor, because a deed copied from older paperwork can carry the wrong numbers. Next, walk every unit with the detector checklist and fix what fails. Then submit the online Resale Certificates application with the smoke certificate attached and ask the Bureau of Zoning when an inspection can happen.

If the building has tenants, tell them when the inspector is coming. If you inherited it, gather the estate papers so your attorney can confirm who signs. A cash buyer can take a two or three family building as it stands, while a buyer using a mortgage will want a clean certificate and an appraisal that supports the price.

Because so many Elizabeth houses have more than one unit, expect the buyer's attorney to ask for each unit's lease, rent roll and deposit records, and to ask whether every kitchen has its own extinguisher and every floor its own carbon monoxide detector. Answering those questions before they are asked is the easiest way to keep the closing date. If a unit was added without a permit, raise it with your attorney early, since it can affect both the certificate and the buyer's financing.

faqs.q: Do I need an inspection to sell my Elizabeth house?
faqs.a: Yes, Elizabeth runs a resale certificate program through an online application, and an occupied house needs its smoke detector certificate attached. Ask the city's Bureau of Zoning for the current fee and the inspection schedule.

faqs.q: What does Elizabeth require for detectors and extinguishers?
faqs.a: Smoke detectors on every level, carbon monoxide detectors on every floor near bedrooms, and a charged 2-A:10-B:C extinguisher within ten feet of the stove in each kitchen. All must be permanently mounted and working.

faqs.q: Which county office records an Elizabeth deed?
faqs.a: The Union County Clerk. Check the block and lot numbers first, because the city issued new ones starting January 1, 2023.

faqs.q: What is the typical home value in Elizabeth?
faqs.a: The median value of an owner-occupied home is $449,300, and only 25.6 percent of homes are owner occupied, so many sales are multifamily buildings.

faqs.q: When is the Elizabeth property tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: April 1, filed with the Union County Board of Taxation, or May 1 where the city has just completed a revaluation. Properties assessed above $1,000,000 may go to the State Tax Court instead.
